both males and women with more masculine gender role identities were more likely to endorse homophobic and heteronormative attitudes, whereas only males with more masculine gender identities and less spiritual meaning were more likely to express homophobia.
both males andfemales who hold a more masculine gender identity, and males who are less involved in gender-typedactivities, score higher on measures of heteronormativity and homophobia.

the role of gender role identity, religiosity, and gender-typed behaviors on attitudes toward homosexuality.
the role of gender role and gender role conflict, and religiosity in attitudes toward homosexuality.
the origins of attitudes towards individuals with a homosexual sexual orientation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gender role and religiosity are two important variables to consider when investigating attitudes toward homosexuality.
there is a significant association between masculine gender role identity, religiosity, and attitudes toward homosexuality, and that the association is stronger for males than females.
there is a relationship between gender and attitudes toward homosexuality, and that gender role identity and religiosity are two factors that may explain some of the variance in this relationship.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more masculine a male is, the more likely he is to hold negative attitudes toward gays.

there is an inverse association between attitudes toward homosexuality and gender role identity.

there is an important relationship between religiosity and attitudes towards homosexuality among both men and women.
